title: Edge node boottrace scratchpad
content:
Objective:
Quick, repeatable breadcrumbs for diagnosing edge node boot failures seen in the field fleet (PXE & cloud images). This is a scratchpad — not a runbook, just commands + observed outputs, hypotheses, and next steps we tried during incident windows.

Summary of observed symptom:
- Node reaches cloud-init complete then kernel drops to emergency.target (initramfs) or systemd fails to start kubelet/ctr due to overlayfs mount errors.
- Node sometimes shows healthy agent in cloud console but never registers with cluster (NotReady).
- Failures have two flavors: (A) early boot storage/mount errors (overlay, ext4 corruption) and (B) networking/CNI init errors (flannel/weave/containerd network namespaces).

Commands run (ordered by time, copy/paste friendly):
- ip a; ip r; cat /etc/resolv.conf
- sudo journalctl -b -u cloud-init -o short-iso | tail -n 80
- sudo journalctl -b -u kubelet -o short-iso | sed -n '1,200p'
- sudo journalctl -b -k | tail -n 200  # kernel messages for fs/cgroup errors
- sudo dmesg | tail -n 120
- lsblk -f; sudo blkid; mount | grep overlay || true
- sudo systemctl status containerd --no-pager
- sudo crictl ps -a || sudo ctr -n k8s.io containers list
- sudo cat /var/log/cloud-init-output.log | sed -n '1,200p'
- sudo cat /etc/fstab || true
- journalctl -b _SYSTEMD_UNIT=systemd-remount-fs.service

Representative error snippets captured:
- "overlay: mounting failed: Operation not permitted"
- "containerd: failed to start service: failed to create snapshotter overlayfs: permission denied"
- "kubelet: failed to register node: node "edge-24" not found" (followed by endless retries)
- "systemd[1]: Failed to mount /var/lib/containerd/io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.overlayfs"
- cloud-init: "Module net: ERROR - Device eth0 not found"

Hypotheses and quick checks:
- Hypothesis A (storage overlayfs kernel module missing or built without CONFIG_OVERLAY_FS): check uname -a and module list. Command: uname -a; sudo lsmod | grep overlay; sudo modprobe overlay && echo OK || echo FAIL
- Hypothesis B (booted in user namespaces disabled mode or containerd configured with rootless bits): check /proc/sys/user/max_user_namespaces and containerd config.
- Hypothesis C (corrupt image or missed cloud-init step writing fstab causing duplicate mounts): compare /var/log/installer and cloud-init-output logs.
- Hypothesis D (PXE initramfs missing exfat/overlay support for certain kernel revisions): correlate bad hosts with kernel version.

Working mitigations tried on a repro node:
- chroot into initramfs, fsck -y on suspected block, reboot — in 2/3 reboots node came back but service flakiness remained.
- Rebuild image with CONFIG_OVERLAY_FS compiled; deploy to 2 nodes -> both registered cleanly.
- Temporary workaround: switch containerd snapshotter to "native" or btrfs on problematic fleet image. Not ideal.

Helm/cluster provisioning notes (where relevant):
- cluster-autoscaler and node-termination-handler were not the issue here (nodes fail before join).
- When testing with kubeadm join, certificate/token flow completed but kubelet failed to create pod infra due to snapshotter overlay error: reproduce with kubeadm init/join logs + kubelet logs.
- Helm charts we deploy that modify sysctl or install a CNI daemonset: helm --namespace kube-system upgrade --install calico enterprise-calico ./charts/calico -f values-edge.yaml (note: sometimes calico init fails if host netns unavailable).

Debugging checklist (fast):
1) Confirm kernel version + overlay module: uname -r; lsmod | grep overlay; modinfo overlay
2) Check container runtime snapshotter config: sudo cat /etc/containerd/config.toml | sed -n '1,200p'
3) Validate mounts + fstab: mount | grep -E 'overlay|containerd|var/lib' ; cat /etc/fstab
4) cloud-init: tail -n 200 /var/log/cloud-init-output.log ; look for network cfg successes
5) CNI: ip link show; crictl logs <pause-pod> or journalctl -u calico-node -n 200
6) If in initramfs, run fsck and inspect /proc/cmdline for boot args

Notes to self / observations to preserve:
- Two distinct fleets: PXE-legacy images (kernel 5.4.x) more likely to hit overlay errors; newer cloud images (5.10+) rarely fail.
- Some vendors ship kernels without user_namespaces enabled which interacts badly with rootless snapshotters.
- Telemetry: add kernel version and overlay module presence to node-boot logs (agent) so fleet can be filtered automatically.

Next steps / tickets to open:
- Rebuild and roll a small canary image with overlay enabled and hardened fstab handling (PLT-5120).
- Add agent-level early-boot probe to capture `lsmod | grep overlay` and `cat /proc/cmdline` into instance metadata (ask infra-sre).
- Add a repro job in infra-ci to boot the PXE image in a VM matrix of kernels 5.4/5.10/5.15 and run kubeadm join + simple pod creation test.

Quick references (commands to paste into ssh session):
- sudo journalctl -b -u kubelet -o cat | sed -n '1,200p'
- sudo crictl info || sudo ctr -n k8s.io info
- sudo dmesg | egrep -i 'overlay|aufs|snapshot' --color=never | tail -n 40

If I forget: prioritize kernel+overlay checks first (fast), then containerd snapshotter config, then cloud-init network bits.

End of scratchpad.

-- Maya
